title: VTC Members Removal Notice — payload
description: A community tells a member it removed them, on whose authority, when, and why. Unsolicited: unlike vtc/members/self-remove-receipt this answers no request from the member, because the member did not ask.

did.description: The removed member's DID — the notice's recipient. Carried in the payload as well as the envelope so that a forwarded notice, detached from its transport, still names its subject.

code.description: Which removal happened. `adminRemoved` is a policy-governed removal by an administrator; `purged` is a forceful super-administrator deletion that skips the removal policy. The two differ in what recourse a member has, which is why they are distinguishable rather than a single `removed`.

disposition.description: How the member's published record was handled. Always concrete — a community resolves any `policydefault` preference before sending, since a notice naming an unresolved default tells the member nothing about their own record.

reason.description: The operator's stated reason, verbatim. OPTIONAL because a community may remove without giving one — but omitting it and sending an empty string are different claims, and a community that has a reason SHOULD send it. This is the member's only account of why.

decidedAt.description: When the removal took effect. Distinct from the notice's own `issuedAt`, which may be much later if the member was offline — and it is the decision, not the delivery, that a member or a third party needs to place in time.

decidedBy.description: DID of the administrator who decided. Names the deciding authority rather than the community, because 'the community removed me' is not answerable and 'this administrator removed me' is. The community itself is the document's `issuer`.
